title: Grove's Uniswap V3 activity is fenced by governance-set tick bounds, price-impact caps and a TWAP window
content:
Four `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`-only setters bound how the Liquidity Layer may touch a Uniswap V3 pool. `setUniswapV3PoolMaxTickDelta` (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.1.4) "bounds the maximum tick movement permitted when swapping through the pool, constraining the acceptable price impact of a swap." `setUniswapV3AddLiquidityLowerTickBound` and `...UpperTickBound` (A...1.5, A...1.6) "constrain[] the lower end" and the upper end "of the price range within which the Grove Liquidity Layer may add liquidity." `setUniswapV3TwapSecondsAgo` (A...1.7) "defines the length of the time-weighted average price window used when the contract consults the pool for pricing."

Together these encode a specific threat model. The **tick delta cap** is anti-sandwich and anti-fat-finger: a swap that would move the pool beyond the permitted range reverts rather than executing at a manipulated price. The **tick bounds** stop a relayer from concentrating liquidity at an absurd price range, which is how an LP position gets drained by a range chosen badly or maliciously. The **TWAP window** ensures pricing decisions read an average rather than the instantaneous spot price, which is what a flash-loan manipulation moves.

The division of labour is the notable part. These are all set by the **admin — Sky Governance via the Grove Proxy** (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1.1) — while the actual swapping and liquidity provision is done by relayers Grove controls. Grove chooses when and how much; Sky Governance defines the envelope within which those choices must fall.

The bounds validation is mutually referential — the lower bound must be strictly less than the current upper, and the upper strictly greater than the current lower — so the pair can never be set into an empty or inverted range, and each change is checked against live state rather than in isolation.
description: Admin-only parameters constrain the price range where liquidity may be added, the maximum tick movement a swap may cause, and the length of the averaging window used to price the pool.
